Surgical resection is the preferred treat- ment if feasible. Palliative or cytoreductive surgery is ben- eficial in hepatic metastases from neuroendocrine tumours because of their slow growth.21 Combined resection and adjuvant chemotherapy (hepatic arterial or systemic) is un- der investigation for colorectal liver metastases. Unresect- able colorectal liver metastases have been treated with sys- temic or hepatic intra-arterial chemotherapy, with modest survival benefits.22 Neoadjuvant chemotherapy, given ei- ther systemically or intra-arterially, has also shown some promise in rendering metastatic colorectal cancer resecta- ble.23 1.
